description: Add a node reached over SSH. The daemon scans the host key of host:port and requests the add pinned to that key; you cannot pass a key, a fingerprint or a credential file. A request from an MCP client always waits for a person, who sees the host, the users, the credential references and the key's SHA-256 fingerprint and approves it; no node exists until then. Ask the user to review it with `sm approvals --plan` or the TUI; once approved, set it up with infra_setup_node. The default policy does not grant this; it needs a policy rule for type:mcp for node.add. Note it makes the daemon dial the host you name.

admin_credential_ref.description: secret://<name> holding the admin_user SSH private key. A person stores it first with: sm secrets import --name <name>; you cannot create or list secrets, so ask the user for the name. Required on a server instance; omit it on a local instance to use the SSH agent

admin_user.description: existing account used once, by the setup, to prepare the node

host.description: DNS name or IP address of the SSH endpoint

user.description: automation user the control plane creates and uses, default supermgmt

description: Plan and submit the setup of a node (id or exact name) with safe parameters only: no Docker access, no service grants, journal logs. The resulting node can be probed and its logs read, but has no service verbs (start, stop, restart) until a person runs `sm nodes setup <node> --unit <unit>`. Only a node without a setup and not behind a tunnel is accepted: re-running setup replaces grants and docker access, so a person does it. A request from an MCP client always waits for a person. The default policy does not grant this; it needs a policy rule for type:mcp granting node.setup and sudoers.write.
